newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda warns of more violence as priest is buried.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda warns of more violence as priest is buried.

text.p: Rwanda's interior minister warned of increased violence and instability in the country as a Canadian priest murdered at the weekend was buried on Monday in the north-western town of Ruhengeri.
"What we are seeing is an increase in violence, not just against expatriates but also against Rwandans," Interior Minister Alexis Kanyarawenge told Reuters.
"Father Pinard was the victim of one such attack and we think we will be seeing more of this," he said.
Guy Pinard, a 61-year-old Roman Catholic priest from the White Fathers order, was buried in the graveyard of Ruhengeri cathedral on Monday afternoon.
A native of Trois Rivieres in Canada's Quebec province, Pinard had been in Rwanda since 1962.
He was gunned down on Sunday as he celebrated communion at his parish church in Kampanga village, 20 km (12 miles) north of Ruhengeri.
Witnesses said Pinard was shot in the back by a lone gunman.
Rwandan state radio reported that the attacker had been recognised by members of the congregation who had tried to apprehend him before he fled.
"We have somebody with us in custody but cannot say more about the investigation," the interior minister said.
Diplomatic sources said the assailant was believed to be a teacher and former member of the Rwandan Patriotic Army (RPA), the current government army.

If true, this would weaken suggestions from government circles that Pinard was killed by Hutu extremists forced back from their refugee camps in Zaire late last year and blamed for a spate of recent murders in the northwest.
The interior minister also pointed the finger at the hardline Hutus who fled Rwanda after committing genocide against minority Tutsis in 1994.

"This increasing instability has been going on since the beginning of the year, and involves former Hutu government soldiers and militiamen who have returned from Zaire with the refugees," Kanyarawenge said.
Three Spanish aid workers were killed and an American citizen wounded in an attack in Ruhengeri two weeks ago.
Those killings followed six separate incidents of violence against expatriates in the preceding week.

The diplomatic sources said that Pinard had been critical of both the current and former governments and had helped both Tutsis and moderate Hutus to flee the 1994 genocide in which about 800,000 people died.
Pinard's body had lain earlier in an open coffin at the diocesan residence in Ruhengeri. It showed few marks of violence although his head was bandaged.
More than 400 people, including fellow missionaries, nuns, local people and Rwandan soldiers packed the cathedral.

"He was assassinated in his church," said Juliusz Janusz, the Pope's ambassador (nuncio) to Rwanda, who led the service. "We hope that after 35 years of service to this country his death might help bring peace."

Pinard's death was first announced by Pope John Paul, who told pilgrims in St Peter's Square in the Vatican on Sunday the priest had been "barbarically assassinated this morning while celebrating mass at his parish church."
"Let us pray to the Holy Virgin for him, for those who are dear to him and for his people, that they may again find peace and respect for life", the pontiff added.
Monday's funeral procession was headed by a White Father bearing a cross marked simply "Father Guy Pinard. Missionary of Africa. Rest In Peace."
